name: Pale Purplish Vinaceous
lede: Pale Purplish Vinaceous is a pale, greyed pink with a violet lean, another step in Ridgway's 1912 "vinaceous" family of wine-toned pinks.

sections.title: Next to its sibling vinaceous
sections.body:
This shade is plate XXXIX, hue 1''', tone f, of Ridgway's 1912 color standards, read from a scan of an aged plate [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system lists the same area as block 4, "light pink," about 3.8 units off [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[light-brownish-vinaceous]], [[silver-pink]], [[hydrangea-pink]] and [[shell-pink]], at 3.6, 3.7, 
Our own library files it as an obscure, qualified name, meaning it exists mainly to subdivide the vinaceous range rather than to mark anything new [1]. The closest of our common colors is [[silver]], 9.3 units away [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, this pink appears in 186, about 0.78 percent, more common than 63 percent of our named colors [2]. It is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 3.3 times the expected rate, and inside a painting it is most often a light [2].

[[painter:john-singer-sargent|John Singer Sargent]] is its most devoted painter, present in 9 of 287 works here, 3.7 times his museums' baseline [2]. The earliest match is a 1500 painting, over four centuries before Ridgway's 1912 name, so that early hit is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a trace of this named pink, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].

origin.named_after: undocumented; a subdivision of Ridgway's vinaceous (wine-toned) pinks

disambiguation.gloss: the neighboring Ridgway vinaceous step, slightly more grey and less violet
